title: Aude Diagnostics – Internal Data-Integrity Dashboard
summary: An internal diagnostics web app, built as a Next.js monolith, that reads straight from the database, verifies the main product is producing correct data for every client, and puts the health of all of them on one screen built for troubleshooting.
overview: Aude's main application generates data for many clients, and the team had no single place to confirm that data was correct for all of them at once.

I built a separate internal web application — a Next.js monolith — that talks directly to the database, checks the main app's output per client, and surfaces the results in one dashboard aimed squarely at the engineers who debug it.
problem: There was no fast way to tell whether the main application was generating correct data across every client, so verifying an issue meant checking clients one at a time.
solution: A dedicated diagnostics dashboard that reads from the database directly, evaluates per-client data integrity, and presents the whole picture in a layout designed for troubleshooting rather than for general reporting.

howItWorks.title: Direct database checks
howItWorks.description: The app queries the database directly and evaluates whether the main application is producing correct data for each client.

howItWorks.title: One-glance dashboard
howItWorks.description: Results for every client are laid out so an engineer can see what is not working without drilling in first. The UI is designed for troubleshooting, not general reporting.

howItWorks.title: Shareable deep links
howItWorks.description: Engineers can explore down to a cause and share a URL that reopens exactly the view they were looking at, so a finding travels with a link instead of a screenshot.

howItWorks.title: User's-eye view
howItWorks.description: A view that shows the UI as the end user sees it alongside the API response behind it, so a visual symptom can be traced to the payload that caused it.

buildingProcess.title: Learning the existing product
buildingProcess.description: Spent the first month working in the existing Aude product, a Next.js frontend with a Node and Express backend using Redis, fixing bugs across it and mostly on the UI. That built up the understanding of the data flows the diagnostics tool would later have to verify, and led to being given the diagnostics project.

buildingProcess.title: Building the diagnostics app
buildingProcess.description: Built the dashboard as a separate Next.js monolith talking directly to the database, and shaped the interface around how engineers actually debug: broad status first, then drill-down, then a shareable link.

buildingProcess.title: Deploying behind the existing authentication
buildingProcess.description: Containerised the app with Docker, deployed it to AWS, and served it from the same origin as the main application so it could reuse the existing single sign-on instead of introducing a second authentication system.

challenges.challenge: Reusing the main product's existing authentication for a second, separately deployed internal application.
challenges.solution: Deployed the diagnostics app on AWS and served it from the same origin as the main application, so a signed-in engineer carries straight over and is sent to the existing login when they are not.
challenges.lesson: Deployment topology can answer an authentication constraint that would otherwise call for a whole second identity system.

challenges.challenge: The dashboard exposes internal data, so being signed in is not by itself sufficient authorization.
challenges.solution: Layered an authorization check on top of the session so the app only serves authorized members of the engineering team.
challenges.lesson: Authentication and authorization are separate problems, and internal tooling needs both.

features: Per-client data-integrity checks read directly from the database
Troubleshooting-first dashboard showing failures at a glance
Deep linking so a specific investigation can be shared as a URL
User's-eye UI view paired with the API response behind it
Access limited to authorized team members on top of the existing single sign-on
highlights: Built an internal diagnostics dashboard as a Next.js monolith that verifies per-client data integrity straight from the database.
Designed the interface for engineers: failures visible at a glance, deep-linkable investigations, and a user's-eye view paired with its API response.
Deployed on AWS so it reuses the main product's existing single sign-on, with access restricted to authorized members of the engineering team.
lessonsLearned: How to design an interface around a debugging workflow instead of around the data model.
That deep-linkable state turns an investigation into something a team can share and reproduce.
How deployment topology can resolve an authentication constraint without adding a second identity system.
